06:10, an inspection at 06:40 finds a bearing that needs replacing, so the
outage becomes corrective maintenance under a work order, and the pump is
Unlike the first story, the timestamps are NOT volatile here. For asset.state
the timestamp is the fact itself -- the instant of the transition -- so an
implementation that stamped the moment of sending would produce a valid
event and a wrong down interval. Only event_id and the chain's ids are
volatile, and the chain's STRUCTURE is checked instead.
None of the three events carries a content_hash: data carries no time, so
two identical trips on the same asset would hash the same and a consumer
deduplicating by hash would drop the second (IAES_SPEC.md, asset.state, rule 3).
Checked by tests/test_asset_state_scenario.py, which runs the Python and the
TypeScript scenario. The flow runtimes do not build asset.state yet: neither
lets a flow set the envelope timestamp (implementations.json).

volatile.$comment: Excluded from cross-implementation comparison, with the reason.
volatile.event_id: a fresh UUID per event, by definition
volatile.correlation_id: generated by the event that enters down; the STRUCTURE is checked instead -- every event of the interval carries the same one
volatile.source_event_id: a reference to another event's volatile id; checked as structure
volatile.dataschema: derived from event_type by the SDK
